requirements.original: replace( in template (present) any inpar, in integer index, in integer len, in template (present) any repl ) return any_string_or_sequence type
requirements.canonical: The `replace` predefined function has the syntax replace(in template (present) any inpar, in integer index, in integer len, in template (present) any repl) return any_string_or_sequence type.

examples.text:
replace ('00000110'B, 1, 3, '111'B); // returns '01110110'B
  replace ('ABCDEF'H, 0, 2, '123'H);  // returns '123CDEF'H
  replace ('01AB23CD'O, 2, 1, 'FF96'O); // returns '01ABFF96CD'O
  replace ("My name is JJ", 11, 1, "xx"); // returns "My name is xxJ"
  replace ("My name is JJ", 11, 0, "xx"); // returns "My name is xxJJ"
  replace ("My name is JJ", 2, 2, "x"); // returns "Myxame is JJ", 
  replace ("My name is JJ", 12, 2, "xx"); // produces test case error
  replace ("My name is JJ", 13, 2, "xx"); // produces test case error
  replace ("My name is JJ", 13, 0, "xx"); // returns "My name is JJxx"
  var template charstring v_char1 := pattern "abc[a-z]+", v_char2 := ?;
  replace(v_char1, 2, 2, pattern "x#(1,2)"); // returns pattern "abx#(1,2)"
  replace(v_char2, 2, 2, "ab"); // returns pattern "??ab"

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- replace( in template (present) any inpar, in integer index, in integer len, in template (present) any repl ) return any_string_or_sequence type

requirements.original: This function replaces the substring or subsequence of value inpar at index index of length len with the string or sequence value repl and returns the resulting string or sequence.
requirements.canonical: The `replace` function SHALL replace the substring or subsequence of inpar starting at index index with length len by repl and return the resulting string or sequence.

ambiguity.issue: "value inpar" and "sequence value repl" although C.4.3-s011/s013 allow templates for both parameters.

replace ('00000110'B, 1, 3, '111'B); // returns '01110110'B
  replace ('ABCDEF'H, 0, 2, '123'H);  // returns '123CDEF'H
  replace ('01AB23CD'O, 2, 1, 'FF96'O); // returns '01ABFF96CD'O
  replace ("My name is JJ", 11, 1, "xx"); // returns "My name is xxJ"
  replace ("My name is JJ", 11, 0, "xx"); // returns "My name is xxJJ"
  replace ("My name is JJ", 2, 2, "x"); // returns "Myxame is JJ", 
  replace ("My name is JJ", 12, 2, "xx"); // produces test case error
  replace ("My name is JJ", 13, 2, "xx"); // produces test case error
  replace ("My name is JJ", 13, 0, "xx"); // returns "My name is JJxx"
  var template charstring v_char1 := pattern "abc[a-z]+", v_char2 := ?;
  replace(v_char1, 2, 2, pattern "x#(1,2)"); // returns pattern "abx#(1,2)"
  replace(v_char2, 2, 2, "ab"); // returns pattern "??ab"

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- The repl parameter is allowed to contain a template that shall contain a specific value, pattern or AnyValue without any matching attributes attached to it.

requirements.original: If either the inpar or repl parameter contain a template, the replace function returns a template with the present restriction according to the following rules:
requirements.canonical: If either inpar or repl of `replace` contains a template, the `replace` function SHALL return a template with the present restriction according to the rules of clause C.4.3.
requirements.condition: inpar or repl contains a template

readings: If inpar or repl contains a template, the returned template SHALL always have the present restriction.
If inpar or repl contains a template, the returned template SHALL have the present restriction unless C.4.3-s025 applies (value restriction when inpar refers to a value- or omit-restricted template).
ambiguity.issue: This sentence states the present restriction unconditionally, while C.4.3-s025 requires the value restriction in some cases; the second reading is chosen as canonical intent but the canonical text keeps the stated rule.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- If either the inpar or repl parameter contain a template, the replace function returns a template with the present restriction according to the following rules:

requirements.original: `? length (index..infinity) is returned when both inpar and repl contain AnyValue`
requirements.canonical: If both inpar and repl of `replace` contain AnyValue, `replace` SHALL return `? length (index..infinity)`.
requirements.condition: inpar and repl both contain AnyValue
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- `? length (index..infinity) is returned when both inpar and repl contain AnyValue`

requirements.original: `* length (index..infinity) is returned when inpar contains AnyValueOrNone and repl` contains AnyValue
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `replace` contains AnyValueOrNone and repl contains AnyValue, `replace` SHALL return `* length (index..infinity)`.
requirements.condition: inpar contains AnyValueOrNone and repl contains AnyValue
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- `* length (index..infinity) is returned when inpar contains AnyValueOrNone and repl` contains AnyValue

requirements.original: In all other cases when the AnyValue matching symbol occurs in the repl parameter, it is automatically converted prior to resolving the function evaluation if any of the following conditions is met: To a compatible binary string containing a single AnyElementOrNone if inpar is of a binary string type
requirements.canonical: In all other cases, when repl of `replace` contains AnyValue and inpar is of a binary string type, the AnyValue SHALL be converted, before the function is evaluated, to a compatible binary string containing a single AnyElementOrNone.
requirements.condition: repl contains AnyValue, inpar is of a binary string type, and neither of the two preceding rules applies

readings: AnyValue in repl SHALL be converted to a binary string with a single AnyElementOrNone if inpar is of a binary string type.
AnyValue in repl SHALL be converted only if some further unstated condition is met, the listed items being the conditions.
ambiguity.issue: The lead-in says "if any of the following conditions is met" but the following items are conversion targets with conditions attached; the first reading is chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- In all other cases when the AnyValue matching symbol occurs in the repl parameter, it is automatically converted prior to resolving the function evaluation if any of the following conditions is met: To a compatible binary string containing a single AnyElementOrNone if inpar is of a binary string type

requirements.original: In all other cases when the AnyValue matching symbol occurs in the repl parameter, it is automatically converted prior to resolving the function evaluation if any of the following conditions is met: To pattern "*" if inpar is of a character string type
requirements.canonical: In all other cases, when repl of `replace` contains AnyValue and inpar is of a character string type, the AnyValue SHALL be converted, before the function is evaluated, to pattern "*".
requirements.condition: repl contains AnyValue, inpar is of a character string type, and neither of the two preceding rules applies
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- In all other cases when the AnyValue matching symbol occurs in the repl parameter, it is automatically converted prior to resolving the function evaluation if any of the following conditions is met: To pattern "*" if inpar is of a character string type

requirements.original: To a compatible binary string containing a single AnyElementOrNone if inpar is of a binary string type
requirements.canonical: The AnyValue-to-AnyElementOrNone conversion of repl in `replace` SHALL produce a binary string compatible with the type of inpar.
requirements.condition: inpar is of a binary string type and repl contains AnyValue
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- To a compatible binary string containing a single AnyElementOrNone if inpar is of a binary string type

requirements.original: To pattern "*" if inpar is of a character string type
requirements.canonical: When inpar of `replace` is of a character string type, the converted repl SHALL be pattern "*".
requirements.condition: inpar is of a character string type and repl contains AnyValue
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- To pattern "*" if inpar is of a character string type

requirements.original: The replace function then returns a value that is equal to the following expression: **-** **substr(inpar, 0, index) & repl &** **substr(inpar, index + len, lengthof(inpar) - index - len)**
requirements.canonical: When inpar or repl is a template and neither of the AnyValue rules applies, `replace` SHALL return a value equal to substr(inpar, 0, index) & repl & substr(inpar, index + len, lengthof(inpar) - index - len).
requirements.condition: inpar or repl contains a template

requirements.original: If any of the substr calls in the previous point would yield a template with the ifpresent matching attribute, this attribute is removed before concatenation and added to the final result of the concatenation.

requirements.condition: a substr call yields a template with ifpresent
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- If any of the substr calls in the previous point would yield a template with the ifpresent matching attribute, this attribute is removed before concatenation and added to the final result of the concatenation.

requirements.original: If inpar contains a reference to a template with the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfills the requirements of the present restriction or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record `of, set` `of or array, the` returned value shall have the present restriction.
requirements.canonical: If inpar of `replace` contains a reference to a template with the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfils the requirements of the present restriction, or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array, the value returned by `replace` SHALL have the present restriction.
requirements.condition: inpar refers to a present-restricted template or to a mandatory/unrestricted field

readings: The returned value SHALL have the present restriction if inpar contains (a) a reference to a template with the present restriction, (b) a matching symbol fulfilling the present restriction, or (c) a reference to an unrestricted template field representing a mandatory record/set field or any field of a union, anytype, record of, set of or array.
The returned value SHALL have the present restriction only if inpar contains a reference to a present-restricted template whose content is such a matching symbol or field reference.
ambiguity.issue: Garbled sentence with unclear scope of "a reference to"; the three-alternative reading is chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- If inpar contains a reference to a template with the present restriction, a matching symbol that fulfills the requirements of the present restriction or a reference to an unrestricted template field that represents a mandatory field of a record or set or any field of a union, anytype, record `of, set` `of or array, the` returned value shall have the present restriction.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.4.3 -- `inpar and repl are of different root type;`

requirements.original: `index is less than 0 or greater than lengthof(inpar);`
requirements.canonical: If the index actual parameter of `replace` is less than 0 or greater than lengthof(inpar), an error SHALL occur.
requirements.condition: index < 0 or index > lengthof(inpar)

examples.text:
replace ('00000110'B, 1, 3, '111'B); // returns '01110110'B
  replace ('ABCDEF'H, 0, 2, '123'H);  // returns '123CDEF'H
  replace ('01AB23CD'O, 2, 1, 'FF96'O); // returns '01ABFF96CD'O
  replace ("My name is JJ", 11, 1, "xx"); // returns "My name is xxJ"
  replace ("My name is JJ", 11, 0, "xx"); // returns "My name is xxJJ"
  replace ("My name is JJ", 2, 2, "x"); // returns "Myxame is JJ", 
  replace ("My name is JJ", 12, 2, "xx"); // produces test case error
  replace ("My name is JJ", 13, 2, "xx"); // produces test case error
  replace ("My name is JJ", 13, 0, "xx"); // returns "My name is JJxx"
  var template charstring v_char1 := pattern "abc[a-z]+", v_char2 := ?;
  replace(v_char1, 2, 2, pattern "x#(1,2)"); // returns pattern "abx#(1,2)"
  replace(v_char2, 2, 2, "ab"); // returns pattern "??ab"

requirements.original: encvalue(in template (value) any inpar, in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return bitstring
requirements.canonical: The `encvalue` predefined function has the signature encvalue(in template (value) any inpar, in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return bitstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.1 -- encvalue(in template (value) any inpar, in universal charstring encoding_info := "", in universal charstring dynamic_encoding := "") return bitstring

requirements.original: The encvalue function encodes a value or template into a bitstring.
requirements.canonical: The `encvalue` function IS the predefined function that encodes a value or template into a bitstring.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.5.1 -- The encvalue function encodes a value or template into a bitstring.

requirements.original: When the actual parameter that is passed to inpar is a template, it shall resolve to a specific value (the same restrictions apply as for the argument of the send statement). The returned bitstring represents the encoded value of inpar, however, the TTCN-3 test system need not make any check on its correctness. The optional encoding_info parameter is used for passing additional encoding information to the codec and, if it is omitted, no additional information is sent to the codec. The optional dynamic_encoding parameter is used for dynamic selection of encode attribute of the inpar value for this single encvalue call. The rules for dynamic selection of the encode attribute are described in clause 27.9. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are: - Encoding fails due to a runtime system problem (i.e. no encoding function exists for the actual type of inpar).
requirements.canonical: When the actual parameter passed to the `inpar` formal parameter of `encvalue` is a template, the template SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.condition: the actual parameter passed to inpar is a template

ambiguity.issue: The standard calls `send` an operation (clause 22.2.1); 'send statement' deviates from that term.
